questions.q: Which variable declaration should be your default in modern JavaScript, according to this lesson?
options: const, reserving let only for variables you'll genuinely reassign later
var, because it's the original JavaScript syntax
let, used for every single variable without exception
There is no recommended default — all three are equally fine to default to
questions.explain: const prevents reassignment and makes code easier to reason about; let is reserved for cases that genuinely need reassignment.

questions.q: Why do blockchain libraries store token/wei balances as bigint instead of JavaScript's regular number type?
options: number can't safely represent whole numbers past about 2^53 - 1, and wei balances routinely exceed that
bigint is simply a newer type with no functional difference from number
number cannot store any numeric value larger than 100
bigint runs faster than number for all computations
questions.explain: Wei amounts routinely exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so bigint avoids silent precision loss.

questions.q: What does typeof null return in JavaScript, and why?
options: "object" — a long-standing bug from 1995 that was never fixed because doing so would break too much existing code
"null" — exactly as expected
"undefined" — because null and undefined are treated identically
It throws a runtime error
questions.explain: This is a famous, well-documented JavaScript quirk, not a mistake in your code.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say to avoid var in new code?
options: It has looser scoping rules than let/const that cause real, hard-to-track bugs
var was removed from modern JavaScript and no longer works
var only works with string values
var requires a semicolon while let and const do not
questions.explain: var's function-level (rather than block-level) scoping is a well-known source of bugs in JavaScript.

questions.q: Given let nothingYet; with no value assigned, what does typeof nothingYet return?
options: "undefined"
"null"
"object"
"number"
questions.explain: A declared variable with no assigned value holds the value undefined, and typeof undefined is "undefined".
